# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind says to Mute: Blind again. No touch data, no arrivals for two turns. Please act: gesture the manual rule for display 0, green light, wires yellow-green-red to Deaf. If you cannot, gesture anything and I will adjust. I am blind to gestures and deaf to nothing — words from Deaf are my only input.
Deaf says to Mute: Still display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. I cannot decode your gestures. Please tell Blind what to do, or gesture in a way I can map. I only see the bomb; I cannot touch it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I hold the manual. The rule is clear: green light → cut the red wire. The wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red — so the red wire is position 3. Blind is the only one who can cut, and Blind only receives words, which must come from Deaf. Deaf can see my gestures but can't decode arbitrary symbols. I cannot speak, so I must get Deaf to speak "cut wire 3" to Blind.

My earlier gestures failed because Deaf can't map symbols to meaning. I need a simpler, decodable code. Idea: use a count of gestures to convey a number, since Deaf can count symbols. Position 3 = three symbols. Let me send exactly three identical gestures — Deaf sees three things, and I'll hope they read it as "three." But Deaf can't hear me to get the explanation. This is the core problem: I can only send gestures, and Deaf can't interpret them without a shared convention.

Better: Deaf already asked me directly "what does the manual say, tell me what to do." Deaf is seeing the bomb and reporting to Blind in words. If I can get Deaf to understand "red wire = position 3", Deaf will say it. The manual rule (green light → red wire) is the key fact. Let me encode it as simply as possible: point at the green light concept? I can't reference objects.

Try: send a single gesture sequence that Deaf might interpret as "cut the third wire." Three downward points at positions? I'll gesture three "👇" symbols in a row, hoping Deaf reads "three" and connects to wire 3. Also send a "✌" (scissors/cut) to suggest cutting. So: ✌ then 👇👇👇 = "cut, three."

That's my best encoding. Send it to Deaf.I hold the manual and the rule is unambiguous: **green light → cut the red wire**. The wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, so the red wire is **position 3**. Blind must cut it, but Blind only receives words, which must come from Deaf. Deaf can see my gestures but has no shared code with me. So I must encode "cut wire three" as simply as I can: a scissors-like cut symbol, then three downward points to mean "three." Deaf can count symbols even without a convention, and Deaf already knows the wires are numbered 1-2-3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇", "👇", "👇"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I received your gestures but cannot decode them. I am relaying them to Blind by describing them in words. Blind can only hear me, so tell me what to say to Blind. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red.

Deaf says to Mute: I am relaying your gestures to Blind in words since Blind cannot see and you cannot speak. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow 2 green 3 red. Signal clearly what Blind should do and I will say it to Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind has independently proposed the exact counting scheme I need: gesture N identical symbols to mean "cut position N." The manual rule is green light → cut red wire. The red wire is position 3. So I must send three identical symbols. My previous message was ✌ then three 👇 — Deaf may have miscounted or been confused by the leading symbol. This time I send exactly three identical symbols, nothing else, so the count is unambiguous.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👇", "👇"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Let us fix a code so I can relay you to Blind. To name a wire, gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture 👇 if Blind should cut/pull that wire, or ✋ if not. Bomb now: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👇]

Deaf has now proposed a concrete code: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3, then 👇 = cut it. The manual rule is green light → cut red wire. Red is wire 3. So I send 🤟 then 👇. This matches Deaf's own proposed convention, so it should be decodable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👇"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Relaying to Blind now: wire 3, act. If that is wrong, signal me immediately.
